question: Should Crabline unconditionally reject pre-existing POSIX artifact directories owned by another UID, including privileged and containerized runs, or require an explicit migration and recovery path first?
rationale: The stricter UID boundary is security-positive but intentionally changes which existing filesystem layouts can run, and tests cannot determine the accepted upgrade contract.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery
options.body: Keep the ownership requirement, add an actionable preflight or repair path, and prove both fresh-directory and existing-directory behavior.

options.title: Accept immediate breakage
options.body: Land the rejection as-is and explicitly accept that affected installations stop until operators repair directory ownership.

options.title: Defer strict rejection
options.body: Land the other durability fixes while postponing the ownership rule until its migration contract is defined.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the ownership requirement, add an actionable preflight or repair path, and prove both fresh-directory and existing-directory behavior.
